chapter: Jazz opinions, Jelly Roll and the Rhythm Club
title: Jazz everywhere: the Graphonola and no regional centers
summary: He played jazz before hearing New Orleans or Chicago music, from a Graphonola, and agrees jazz started everywhere.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: Kansas City?
I was playing jazz music before I heard any jazz music from New Orleans or Chicago, 'cause we had a Graphonola.
Wind it up and play the records. That's the way I - you know.
Where were the records from that you were listening to?
I don't know the names. I remember one...
That was a composition played by a jazz band?
Wasn't no jazz music to me. They was just playing.
Who recorded that?
I do not know. My sister bought a Graphonola, not a Graphophone. You'd just buy your records and put it on there. The bulldog was listening.
What about the cylinders? Do you remember machines that used to play the records that were cylinders. The records weren't on discs but they were on a cylinder.
No, I don't know anything about that. The only one I know you wind up -
Like the old Bluebird labels and all those things.
Yeah.
There was a professor at Howard University that said that jazz didn't start anywhere particularly, it was just happening all over. Eubie Blake told me the same thing.
I agree with that!
Eubie Blake told me that he heard jazz in Baltimore, Maryland, in 1900. Do you go along with that?
Yes I will. I just got through saying that I didn't know nothing about no jazz music from New Orleans or Chicago jazz.
They didn't talk about regions of jazz or jazz centers or stuff like that?
Say it again.
They didn't have jazz centers or something like everybody said, let's go to New Orleans 'cause that's where it come from?
No.
They never said anything about, let's go to Chicago?
They never said anything about it, never did.
They never said anything about going to Kansas City either?
No, never heard it, never did.
